target_claim: Theorem 1 (solution lines 0042-0043): 'When Dijkstra's algorithm processes Gn starting from source s, it performs Omega(2^n) successful Relax operations' -- with the algorithm model the solution itself names on lines 0097-0099, 'Dijkstra's algorithm with a modified priority queue that allows re-insertion'. The subsidiary claim on lines 0114-0116 that t alone receives Omega(2^{n-1}) relaxations is tested too.
failing_input: G_n as defined verbatim on solution lines 0017-0035, for every n >= 5; headline witness n=20 (|V|=40). Also refuted at every n in [5,25] and, by exhaustive search over ALL admissible priority-queue tie-breaking orders, at every n in [2,9].
observed_vs_claimed: CLAIMED: successful Relax count on G_n is Omega(2^n), i.e. exists c>0 with count(n) >= c*2^n for all large n; and >= 2^{n-1} successful relaxations at t alone. OBSERVED (exact integer counters, no wall clock): successful(n) = 4n - 5 exactly for every n in [5,25] under the primary reading (lazy re-insertion queue, low-index tie-break). n=4:11, n=6:19, n=8:27, n=10:35, n=12:43, n=14:51, n=16:59, n=18:67, n=20:75, n=25:95 -- constant first difference of 4. Total Relax INVOCATIONS (successful or not) at n=20 is only 76, and successful relaxations at t is 1, not 2^{n-1}=524288. Ratio successful(n)/2^n falls monotonically 6.88e-01 (n=4) -> 1.05e-01 (n=8) -> 1.05e-02 (n=12) -> 4.73e-04 (n=16) -> 7.15e-05 (n=20), so no constant c>0 exists. Measured under 5 tie-break rules x 2 stale-entry policies (all linear: 4n-5, 2n-1, or 4n-5 variants; the largest is 4n-5). ADVERSARIAL ORACLE: exhaustive search over every admissible execution order of the stated re-insertion variant gives MAX successful = 4n-5 as well (n=2:3, 3:7, 4:11, 5:15, 6:19, 7:23, 8:27, 9:31, all exhaustive) -- so no tie-breaking whatsoever can rescue the bound. Constants are fully visible: measured 4n-5 vs. required c*2^n. MECHANISM: every edge leaving v_{i,b} carries the same weight (the weight function depends only on the tail vertex), hence d[v_{i,0}] = d[v_{i,1}] at every level; the negative branch -2^i+1 is simultaneously the cheapest continuation AND the minimum key, so the priority queue pops the all-ones (optimal) prefix FIRST at every level. Each label attains its final value on its first successful relaxation and never strictly decreases again, so no cascade of re-relaxations occurs. An exponential counterexample requires the optimal path to be discovered LAST; this construction has the sign structure backwards. Brute-force cross-check confirms the re-insertion Dijkstra's distances equal the exhaustive-enumeration shortest distances at every vertex for n=2..14, i.e. the algorithm is not even tricked into a wrong answer on this family.
faithfulness_notes: The construction is fully specified and was implemented verbatim from lines 0017-0035: s -> v_{1,0}, v_{1,1} at weight 0; for 1<=i<=n-2, v_{i,0} -> v_{i+1,b} at +2^i and v_{i,1} -> v_{i+1,b} at -2^i+1 for both b; v_{n-1,b} -> t at weight 0. |V| = 2n (the solution itself writes '1 + 2(n-1) + 1 = 2n = O(n)' on line 0023, conflating 2n with n; measurement is reported against both n and |V| and the refutation is unaffected since 4n-5 is linear in either). Verified mechanically: G_n is a DAG (Kahn) for all tested n and contains negative edges for n>=3 (at n=2 the middle-level edge set is empty, so G_2 has no negative edge at all -- a further defect of the family, noted but not load-bearing). The Relax operation is implemented exactly as Definition 1 (lines 0013-0016): update d[v] iff d[v] > d[u]+w(u,v), and 'successful' means d[v] was updated. The algorithm model is the one the solution names on lines 0097-0099 -- a priority queue permitting re-insertion on decrease; because the solution gives no pseudocode, BOTH standard readings were measured (skip stale entries on pop, and process every popped entry) across five tie-break rules, and additionally an exhaustive search over all admissible pop orders, so the verdict does not depend on any implementation choice left open by the text. All arithmetic is exact Python int; floats appear only in printed display ratios and decide nothing. No sampling except the 'rand' tie-break rule, which uses a fixed seed (12345). Nothing in the solution was repaired or supplied by me: the claimed Key Observation (line 0081-0083) that v_{k+1,b} is updated once per each of the 2^k paths is directly contradicted by the measurement, since edge weights depending only on the tail make all 2^k prefixes collapse to a single label value per level.
